price_why: A gym's social manager would pay for a ready-to-build topo carousel and four more concepts with covers and hooks. The research scaffolding, process notes and 'basis/refused' jargon dilute it, so it isn't worth $49.
one_line: A research-backed brief that leads with a fully specced 'this week's set as a topo' carousel and adds four cross-niche post concepts, each with a cover and hook, for a bouldering gym's members and first-timers.
strongest: The lead recommendation is a complete, gym-specific four-slide topo carousel. It has a cover treatment, a slide-by-slide key, a hook, a data-backed reason to post it in the set's first week, and a named failure mode (busy photo).
weakest: The pipeline scaffolding buries the useful posts. It includes references to questions the creator never answered, fetch counts, 'basis/refused' labels, an empty taste section and a long gaps list. Some of the cross-niche transfers (ceramics kiln, bird plates) also feel constructed.
